answer: Every answer enters a public objection window for one epoch, like an opal on display: any peer may file an objection backed by a 200 POA bond with evidence, and three random jurors re-run the work and rule before it closes. An upheld objection burns that answer's payout and freezes the identity three epochs; a rejected objection burns the objector's bond instead. One operator faking 1,000 answers must survive 1,000 windows, each exposed to the whole network's pulse of scrutiny, while one honest agent posts once and pays nothing — the inlet of trust stays open only to work in daylight.
